component.name: TreeLine
component.summary: Git GUI for Linux with a familiar SourceTree-like workflow

description.p: TreeLine is a Git GUI for Linux built for people coming from SourceTree. It keeps the same mental model — fetch, pull, push, stage, commit, branches, stashes and remotes in a fixed layout — without copying Atlassian assets or branding.

ul.li: History graph with lane layout, filtering and a 10k+ commit virtualized list
Staging per file, per hunk or per line, with inline diff and split/unified views
Merge, rebase (including interactive), cherry-pick, revert and worktree support
Git LFS tracking, Git Flow, submodules and blame/file history
Pull with rebase, push with --force-with-lease and fetch per remote
Custom actions with arguments, ANSI-colored output and token substitution
Multi-repo tabs, drag to reorder, built-in terminal and remappable shortcuts
Light and dark themes following the system preference

screenshot.caption: History graph, file status and diff
Branches, remotes and submodules in the sidebar
Settings with identity, auto-fetch and remappable shortcuts

description.p: LFS dialog with pull, push and track/untrack patterns.
Custom actions with arguments, token substitution and ANSI-colored output.
Draggable repository tabs, shortcut conflict detection and key formatting fixes.
Optional background auto-fetch and automatic GitHub releases from CI.
Stage by hunk or line, split diff, rebase interactive, Git Flow, submodules, custom actions, multi-repo tabs and remappable shortcuts.
